chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Wahb al-Hariri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The buyer of the real estate receives sustenance, and the seller of it is annihilated.

key_terms.الْعُقْدَةِ: Real estate / Property (specifically land or a defined plot)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence for the buyer and seller of real estate according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contrasts the spiritual states of the buyer and seller of 'urqah' (often interpreted as a specific plot of land or a metaphor for the world), promising sustenance (marzooq) to the former and annihilation (mamhoq) to the latter. This dichotomy reflects the Shia scholarly view that acquiring property for legitimate use brings divine provision, whereas selling it—particularly if done with greed or neglect of rights—leads to the erosion of one's spiritual and material blessings. The terminology underscores the transient nature of worldly transactions compared to the enduring reality of divine decree.
